```{r check-library-functions, echo=FALSE}
check_install = function(packages) {
   not_installed = setdiff(packages, rownames(installed.packages()))
   if(length(not_installed) > 0) {
      write(paste("The libraries", not_installed, "are not installed, aborting.",
                   sep=" "), stdout())
      stop()
   }
}
```

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Avoid StartupMessages
shhh <- suppressPackageStartupMessages
```

```{r load-libraries, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
packages = c("tidyverse","Seurat", "AnnotationHub", "janitor",
             "reshape", "DT","cowplot","patchwork","forcats","SeuratDisk")

check_install(packages)
installed = lapply(
```

```{r}
# Directory paths
data_dir <- file.path(params$outputDir, "data",Sys.Date(), params$sample_name)

invisible(mapply(
    FUN = dir.create,
    list(data_dir),
    MoreArgs = list(recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
))
```

```{r}
# Load the dataset
# Initialize the Seurat object with the raw (non-normalized data).
  seurat.data <- Read10X(data.dir = params$matricesDir)
  seurat <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = seurat.data, project = "Atherosclerosis_bg_aortas", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)
  seurat[["total_reads"]] <- Matrix::colSums(GetAssayData(seurat,slot = "counts"))
  seurat[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(seurat, pattern = "^mt-")
  seurat[["novelty"]] <- log10(seurat$nFeature_RNA)/log10(seurat$nCount_RNA)
  saveRDS(seurat,file = file.path(data_dir,paste0("seurat_", Sys.Date(),".rds")))
```


The initial dataset after cellranger filtering and seurat initial filtering (a gene must have expression in at least 3 cells and a cell has to have at least 200 genes) has `r ncol(seurat)` cells.

```{r}
initial_cells <- ncol(seurat)
```


# QC Plots {.tabset}

## nGenes

With the distribution of the number of genes we observe that most cells have a very
low number of genes. We set a low threshold (red line)of `r params$minGenes` 
number of Genes.

### Histogram

```{r}
ggplot(data = seurat[[]], aes(x = nFeature_RNA)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 50) + geom_vline(xintercept = params$minGenes, col = "red", linetype = "dashed") + xlab("nGenes")
```

### Violin Plot

```{r}
VlnPlot(seurat, features = "nFeature_RNA") + geom_hline(yintercept = params$minGenes, col = "red", linetype = "dashed")
```

### Ranked distribution
 
```{r}
nGenes_df <- seurat[[]] %>% as.data.frame() %>% tibble::rownames_to_column(var  = "barcode") %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(barcode, nFeature_RNA)) %>% dplyr::arrange(-nFeature_RNA)
nGenes_df$ranked_bc <- as.integer(rownames(nGenes_df))
```

```{r}
p <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = nGenes_df, aes(x = ranked_bc, y = nFeature_RNA), col = "red")

p  +
  scale_y_continuous(trans='log10') + geom_hline(yintercept = params$minGenes, col = "red", linetype = "dashed") + ylab("nGenes - log10") + xlab("barcode")
```


## nUMIs

Similarly to the number of genes, we try to capture the majority of cells.
Red line indicated the minimum  threshold. `r params$minUMIs` number of UMIs.

### Histogram

```{r}
ggplot(data = seurat[[]], aes(x = nCount_RNA)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 50)  + geom_vline(xintercept = params$minUMIs, col = "red", linetype = "dashed") + xlab("nUMIs") + xlim(0,5000)
```

### Violin Plot

```{r}
VlnPlot(seurat, features = "nCount_RNA") + geom_hline(yintercept = params$minUMIs, col = "red", linetype = "dashed") 
```

### Ranked distribution

```{r}
nUMIs_df <- seurat[[]] %>% as.data.frame() %>% tibble::rownames_to_column(var  = "barcode") %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(barcode, nCount_RNA)) %>% dplyr::arrange(-nCount_RNA)
nUMIs_df$ranked_bc <- as.integer(rownames(nUMIs_df))
```

```{r}
p <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = nUMIs_df, aes(x = ranked_bc, y = nCount_RNA), col = "red")

p  +
  scale_y_continuous(trans='log10') + geom_hline(yintercept = params$minUMIs, col = "red", linetype = "dashed") + ylab("nUMIs - log10") + xlab("barcode")
```

## Mitochondrial percentage

We observe a rather high mitochondrial percentage on some cells. As this is a 
heart sample, we use a higher thresholds of `r params$maxMitoPer`.


```{r}
ggplot(data = seurat[[]], aes(x = percent.mt)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 1) + xlim(0,100) + geom_vline(xintercept = params$maxMitoPer, col = "red", linetype = "dashed")
```

```{r}
VlnPlot(seurat, features = "percent.mt") + geom_hline(yintercept = params$maxMitoPer, col = "red", linetype = "dashed")
```

## Genes detected per cell

We observe that, in average, the cells have over `r median(seurat$nFeature_RNA)`
(10^`r round(median(log10(seurat$nFeature_RNA)),2)`).

```{r}
seurat[[]] %>% 
        ggplot(aes(x=orig.ident, y=log10(nFeature_RNA), fill=orig.ident)) + 
        geom_boxplot() + 
        ggtitle("NGenes")
```

## nUMIs vs nGenes

Using this plot we can assess whether there is a large population of low quality cells with low counts and/or gene detection. The data points are colored by the mitochondrial content to see if there is some correlation.

We observe a correct tendency with some outlier cells. The applied 
filters will remove them.

```{r}
seurat[[]] %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log10(nCount_RNA), y = log10(nFeature_RNA),color = percent.mt)) + scale_color_gradient(limits=c(0, 100)) +
  geom_point() + 
  stat_smooth(method = lm) + 
  facet_wrap(~orig.ident) + xlab("log10 nUMis") + ylab("log10 nGenes")
```


## Novelty

Novelty representes cells that have less genes detected per count than other cells. We can see that in general we have high novelty.

```{r}
    seurat[[]] %>%
    ggplot(aes(x=novelty))+
  geom_histogram(bins = 50) 
```


# Filtering

Filters used:

* minGenes: `r params$minGenes`
* minUMIs: `r params$minUMIs`
* maxMitoPer: `r params$maxMitoPer`
* minNovelty: `r params$minNovelty`


```{r}
seurat <- subset(seurat, subset = nFeature_RNA > params$minGenes & percent.mt < params$maxMitoPer & nCount_RNA >params$minUMIs & novelty > params$minNovelty) 
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = seurat[[]], aes(x = nFeature_RNA)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 50) + xlab("nGenes")
```


```{r}

```

# Conclusions QC

From the `r initial_cells` initial cells, `r ncol(seurat)` passed the filtering 
(`r round(ncol(seurat)*100/initial_cells,2)`%).
